title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015; the preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI for this sensitivity analysis is [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide explicit artifact pointers and checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and to assist NetOps at scale. Operational NetOps requires not only syntactic plausibility but demonstrable functional correctness, bounded blast radius (limited collateral impact) and strong provenance. A common architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes candidate device changes; a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants and high‑level policies; an automated repair subroutine attempts to correct violations. Prior tool‑assisted critique and verifier work (e.g., CRITIC) motivates such pipelines but there is limited preregistered, within‑task paired evidence isolating the verifier effect with full provenance. We therefore ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? To answer this we preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3), executed it end‑to‑end with archival of inputs, outputs, verifier traces, provider calls and analysis artifacts, and report the preregistered confirmatory analysis and prespecified sensitivity evaluations with deterministic reproduction guidance.
sections.related_work: LLM→IaC and intent translation literature (PreConfig; intent engines) demonstrates feasibility of LLM proposals but highlights correctness and safety gaps. Tool‑assisted critiquing and verifier‑guided repair (CRITIC; tool‑interactive critiquing) show verifiers can reduce semantic errors in code and configuration generation. Deterministic NetOps verifiers and ensemble verification (SymNet, ensemble approaches) provide foundations for fast functional checks. Recent surveys of LLMs for NetOps and intent translation identify architectural desiderata: verifier coverage, auditable traces, and repair budgets. Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑grounded within‑task paired evaluation isolating the verifier effect with full provenance: archived per‑episode validator traces, provider calls, and analysis artifacts supporting deterministic reproduction of bootstrap CIs and contingency tables.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline) on a per‑task deterministic functional correctness indicator emitted by a deterministic validator. Primary hypothesis H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (power ≈ 80% with 200 pairs under the preregistered discordant assumption). Task generation and inclusion rules. We generated 200 stratified tasks with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 constrained to features covered by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Topology scales were stratified (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata included common features (BGP, OSPF, VLAN, MTU). Tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were automatically detected and excluded (task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Execution adapter and model. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed paired episodes using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Each task used a single shared initial generation candidate (shared_initial_generation per preregistration). Guarded condition semantics. Guarded episodes invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5; when violations were flagged the pipeline invoked an automated repair subroutine once (preregistered maximum = 1). The verifier emitted structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) including parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count; these per‑episode traces are archived in execution/scoring/*.json (example hashes given in the Disclosure). Analysis plan and reproducibility. Primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar on complete pairs with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Missingness policy: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) with a prespecified sensitivity 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat both‑missing pairs as failures). All raw per‑episode records, seeds, prompts, provider calls, validator traces and execution logs were archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7). Analysis executor identifier: paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc).
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs included in the primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 above). Primary confirmatory (complete pairs n = 188). Contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e...): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail within complete pairs). Aggregate: baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis_log documents seed and resample count; SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a...). Sensitivity (both_missing → failures). Applying preregistered sensitivity across all 200 pairs yields n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12; guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015. The preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI for this sensitivity analysis—computed by resampling the empirical 200 per‑pair records with replacement (10,000 resamples, seed=1729)—is [0.0, 0.035]. (Rationale: bootstrap resampling of the 200 observed pairs produces N10 ~ Binomial(200, 3/200); percentiles for N10/200 with 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 yield lower bound 0 and upper bound 7/200 = 0.035; the archived analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the exact bootstrap settings.) Repair provenance and mapping. Repair invocations were rare (3). Per the archived execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) each repair invocation is linked to an explicit provider_call filename and its SHA‑256; those three repair records correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). For deterministic verification readers can extract the exact (episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename, provider_call_sha256, final_score) rows from execution/raw_results.jsonl (artifact SHA‑256 above). Representative per‑episode validator traces. Representative scoring JSONs included in the archive (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000001‑guarded.json SHA‑256 = 60f5b7a7..., task‑000002‑guarded.json SHA‑256 = 9d60eda6..., task‑000003‑guarded.json SHA‑256 = 2ff9540d...) show structured validator traces (validation_before/validation_after) with parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count; these substantiate the reported per‑episode success indicators and provide the per‑episode blast‑radius diagnostics used in exploratory reporting. Repair activity and blast radius. Each successful repair reduced a failing shared initial candidate into a validator‑passing final configuration in the guarded condition (n_10 = 3). The verifier traces include observed_touched_field_count and parsed_command_count which serve as per‑episode blast‑radius diagnostics; aggregate blast‑radius statistics were not computed as a preregistered confirmatory estimand because repair invocations were too few for robust inference, but the per‑episode validator traces are archived for follow‑up analyses.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by automated repairs. The effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant (alpha = 0.05). Two operational causes are evident in the archived artifacts: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage / repair budget — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and repair was permitted only once per preregistration, so repairs were rarely invoked (repair stage invocations = 3). Operational implications. Deterministic verifiers add auditability and can correct some LLM mistakes, but measurable operational benefit requires (a) a nontrivial baseline error floor where LLMs make fixable functional mistakes; (b) verifier coverage aligned to prevalent LLM error modes; and (c) a larger repair budget (multiple iterations) to handle multi‑step violations. For settings with very high baseline correctness the primary practical benefit of a verifier may be improved confidence, deterministic provenance and forensicability rather than large absolute gains in success rate. Reviewer‑requested reproducibility additions implemented here. (1) Sensitivity bootstrap CI: computed for the preregistered sensitivity (treat both‑missing pairs as failures) by resampling the empirical 200 per‑pair records with replacement 10,000 times using seed=1729; resulting 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0, 0.035]. The analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc) records the seed and resample count used by the archived executor paired_binary_analysis_v1. (2) Repair provenance mapping: the three repair invocations and their provider_call filenames and SHA‑256 checksums are linked in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); readers can deterministically extract the exact (episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename, provider_call_sha256, final_score) entries from that file. Threats to validity. Internal validity: single shared initial candidate per pair (preregistered), limited retries, and 24 failed episodes reduced the analytic set to 188 complete pairs. Construct validity: the success metric is a deterministic validator‑based functional correctness indicator and depends on verifier coverage and the fidelity of synthetic golden configs. External validity: single‑model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic Cornetto‑like tasks, and limited verifier scope restrict generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) limit power to detect effects smaller than the preregistered 20‑pp threshold. Recommendations. Future studies should (a) increase baseline task difficulty or include tasks outside current verifier coverage to raise LLM error rates; (b) increase repair budgets (multiple automated iterations) and log iterative traces; (c) evaluate multiple LLM families and verifiers; (d) when repair counts permit, compute distributional blast‑radius statistics (observed_touched_field_count) as preregistered estimands.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model ensembles, and repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Models & provider: all generation calls used declared model gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd. Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in Dockerized environments; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 preregistration SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3 was archived prior to observing final execution outputs. Initial master prompt reference (immutable archived path): provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution & analysis provenance: the execution manifest and analysis artifacts record all prompts, raw outputs, verifier traces, parsed IRs, seeds, provider_call filenames and their SHA‑256s, and hashes. Key artifact pointers and checksums (relative paths inside the supplied manuscript evidence bundle): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipe (bootstrap CI and sensitivity). To reproduce the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI (complete pair or sensitivity): 1) load execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7), 2) extract per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) according to the preregistered missingness policy (complete_pair_primary or the sensitivity that treats both‑missing pairs as failures), 3) with seed=1729 draw 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the pairs (indices sampled with replacement), compute Δ per resample, and take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the exact seed and resample count used by paired_binary_analysis_v1 (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc). Per‑repair provenance mapping. The three repair invocations that yielded the three guarded‑only successes are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider_calls directory; execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) links each repair invocation to episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score. The paper provides a compact archival Table 1 copied verbatim from those archived records for deterministic verification; readers can cross‑check the provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s against the provider_calls directory in the published artifact bundle. Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the drafting snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
